main_text.head: IN DISTICHON AB EITZINGERO QVODAM aduersus Reginam Angliæ scriptum
main_text.p: TV, quæ Romanas voluisti spernere leges, Hispano discès subdere colla iugo.
main_text.head: RESPONSIO.
main_text.p: DVra ferox Anglis quum vincla pararet Iberus, Indomitósque truci classe domare viros: Misit tartarei scitatum oracula Ditis. (Sic Magica bellum tutior arte gerit.)
Huic Dæmon, Aio te vincere posse Britannos Et premere immani colla superba iugo.
Arripit has sortes, & sic exponit Iberus, Hispano subdes colla Britanne iugo.
Ast Iber ambigua deceptus sorte, secures Anglorum metuit vincula dura ferens.
Sic regnum Cræsi & magnam peruertit opum vim Dæmon, & Pyrrhum perdidit Æacidem.

page.notes: Printed page number "31" at top right. The ornament at the top and the decorative elements are not transcribed. The Latin verse uses long s and italic; the initial "D" is an enlarged letter joined to "Vra" as printed ("DVra"). Possible doubtful readings: "scitatum" (possibly "scitatum" as printed), "Ditis" and "Pyrrhum" read from the scan. Signature "I.I.B." is printed at the foot after the verse, treated as a closing paragraph.
